content.comment_body: I have a momentary switch connected to a digital input on an older PLC. Someone suggested moving the wires to an analog input and adding another button for an extra function, so I wouldn't have to run additional cables in the garage. Simulation tests for this setup seem to work fine. However, I'm unsure how to wire the button for actual use. Any wiring suggestions are appreciated! EDIT: I'm using the [product_name] analog expansion module.

Hello, I believe your R6 resistor should also be 1k? Having this makes a total of 6k, which would result in 4mA at 24VDC under idle conditions. In theory, your configuration is feasible. But if multiple buttons might be pressed simultaneously, things could become more complex.

Hi, basically, this circuit generates different voltages by using buttons in series (cascade circuit). It'll work as long as the voltage/current to the [product_name] analog module stays within the measured range (0...10V or 0/4...20mA). If only one switch is pressed, the system should function properly. Pressing two or more buttons at once will allow only one button to be detected.

Thank you for the feedback! I noticed that this setup requires three wires (VCC, GND, OUT). If I put the buttons in parallel and use the 0/4...20mA settings with a closed loop circuit as shown in the image below, will this work? [url] (Not sure if it's suitable.)

This configuration can work, but only if you're sure that more than one button won't be pressed at the same time. Set the input to 0-20mA. If multiple buttons are pressed, it becomes impossible to distinguish which input is active. For example, pressing the button with the 4k resistor will produce the same input value as pressing both the 1k and 3k resistors at the same time.

One solution is to use resistors with values such as 1R, 2R, 4R, and 8R in series, along with a base resistor for the voltage output. Attached is an example showing how only one switch can be determined, as combinations will exceed 10V. To detect all combinations, simply lower the value of the base resistor so the combined voltage stays below 10V when all switches are on. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum members are evaluating how several momentary pushbuttons could be connected to a single analog input using the [product_name] analog expansion module to reduce wiring. While simulation shows promising results, users raise concerns about real-world wiring and the ambiguity that arises when more than one button is pressed at the same time. The analog approach could work, but may encounter misdetection and limitations, especially with simultaneous button presses.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants a reliable solution for connecting multiple pushbuttons to a single analog input, minimizing wires while maintaining accurate and clear detection of which button is pressed. Guidance on practical wiring implementation is also expected.
